sentences.text: D.Chandrasekhar vs State Of Ap on 16 September, 2019

Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5169 Of 2019
Order:

1. The petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 3 seek to quash the proceedings against them in C.C. No.823 of 2019, pending on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Palamaner, Chittoor district (for short, 'the trial Court'), which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 188 and 273 of IPC and Section 59(i) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Palamaner, Chittoor district
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that, on 08.03.2019 at 05.30 P.M., on receiving the credible information, the complainant along with his staff conducted vehicle checking in front of RTO office, Chittoor-Bangalore road, Gangavaram mandal, found the petitioners/Accused Nos.1 to 3 illicitly transporting the banned tobacco products through the vehicle bearing registration No.AP 26 BF 9630, without having any bills for their own profit, and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R., and remanded them to judicial custody for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore UDPR,J registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of the Head Constable, Gangavaram Police Station.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed quashing the proceedings against the Petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 3 in C.C. No.823 of 2019,
